haiku-low.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes invoices to the shadow store only.
haiku-low.q2: The new engine charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store only, with no charging.
haiku-low.q3: Seven consecutive nightly results each under 0.1% mismatch, with at least 5,000 invoices compared in total. A person makes the move.
haiku-low.q4: The charge monitor opens a rollback when new-engine charge failure rate exceeds 2% in a 10-minute window. This applies only in both or new_only.
haiku-low.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only, with gates reset. The rollout must pass through shadow again, and earlier comparison results do not count.
haiku-low.q6: Manual rollback from new_only is refused from day 35. Usage events are kept only 35 days, so the oldest skipped event expires and replay cannot finish.
haiku-low.q7: Workers read the billing_mode flag and rollback record before every charge. A charge already sent may finish or be left unknown, and the resolve step settles it.
haiku-low.q8: Gate counters live with the comparison job's results: nightly rows, unresolved mismatches, both start date, and Finance sign-off. The numeric gate cannot be overridden by anyone.
haiku-low.q9: The charge monitor measures new-engine charge failure rate per 10-minute window. When it exceeds 2%, it opens the rollback record.
haiku-low.q10: Charges falling due wait, with none dropped. They are charged in the final catch-up, after the old engine's flag flip and recomputed invoices.
haiku-low.q11: A ledger uniqueness constraint on customer and period, pending reservation, provider idempotency key, and the handover rule skipping charged or pending periods.
haiku-low.q12: Billing is left in RollbackBlocked with the new engine halted, and on-call is paged. On-call finishes remaining steps from the saved step; nothing restarts automatically.

sonnet.q1: The old engine charges and writes the ledger. The new engine reads the same usage events and writes invoices to the shadow store only.
sonnet.q2: The new engine computes, charges and writes the ledger. The old engine computes every invoice into the shadow store only, with no charging.
sonnet.q3: Gate A must be met: 7 consecutive nightly results, each with mismatch rate under 0.1%, and at least 5,000 invoices compared in total across them. A person makes the move (it is never automatic).
sonnet.q4: The charge failure rate of the new engine above 2% over any 10-minute window. This happens only in both and new_only, not in shadow (errors there are recorded only).
sonnet.q5: Every rollback ends in old_only (via RollbackBlocked if a step fails). Gates reset (consecutive days, invoices compared, days in both, Finance sign-off cleared). The rollout must go through shadow again and meet gate A, then gate B with Finance sign-off; earlier comparison results do not count.
sonnet.q6: From day 35 in new_only, manual rollback is refused (allowed through day 34). The document says the oldest skipped usage event expires on day 35 (usage events are kept 35 days), so replay can't be completed. After day 35 decommissioning is allowed and nothing can be rolled back to.
sonnet.q7: Workers read the billing_mode flag in the config service (the source of truth). Before every charge they also read the rollback record. If the config service is unreachable they keep the last known mode, or do not charge and retry if they have none. NOT STATED for what happens to an invoice mid-processing when the mode changes, except that while a rollback record is open the new engine may not start a charge; a charge already sent may finish or be left unknown and the resolve step settles it.
sonnet.q8: Evidence is the nightly comparison result rows, the unresolved-mismatch list, the date both began and the Finance sign-off, stored with the comparison job's results. Nothing can override the numeric gate and no forward move is automatic. A person makes each move, and the gate conditions must be met, otherwise the rollout stays in its mode.
sonnet.q9: The charge monitor. It counts the new engine's charge attempts per 10-minute window and failures. When failures exceed 2% it opens the rollback record, which starts the rollback (run by the rollback worker).
sonnet.q10: Nobody charges between the halt and the final catch-up. Charges that fall due wait and are made in the final catch-up step, when the old engine charges periods with no live ledger entry (after the flag is set to old_only).
sonnet.q11: The ledger has one row per customer and period (uniqueness constraint). The engine writes a pending row before charging, and the row key is the provider's idempotency key. The handover rule means the old engine charges a period only if the ledger has no entry or the entry is not charged; charged or pending are skipped. In-flight or unknown charges are resolved with the provider before the catch-up.
sonnet.q12: The rollback goes to RollbackBlocked and on-call is paged. Nothing restarts automatically and the new engine stays halted. On-call finishes the remaining steps from the step saved in the rollback record, then the rollback closes, gates reset and the mode goes to old_only. The flag's state depends on which step failed (NOT STATED beyond that).
